summary_paragraph: A 58-year-old male with a history of AML in remission following stem cell transplant and chronic extensive sclerodermic skin GVHD was admitted for worsening foot pain and evaluation of a skin GVHD flare. He had no signs of active infection, with negative blood cultures and normal white count. Empiric Zosyn was started but discontinued after no growth was found. Dermatology recommended changes to his topical regimen including clobetasol, silver sulfadiazine, and collagenase ointment. MRI of the right ankle showed no tendonitis or tear, with findings attributed to nonspecific muscle edema and skin changes from GVHD. Liver enzymes were elevated, likely due to antibiotics, and expected to resolve. Pain was controlled with oral oxycodone, and the patient was discharged home after three days with updated wound care instructions and follow-up plans.
